name: Eubulus
title: Christian brother in Rome
summary: Eubulus was a Christian believer in Rome mentioned in Paul's second letter to Timothy. He sent his greetings to Timothy through Paul, who at that time was imprisoned in Rome. Eubulus is mentioned only once in the Bible, but his mention testifies to the Christian community that supported Paul in his final days.

keyEvents.title: Greeting to Timothy
keyEvents.description: Eubulus sends his greetings to Timothy through Paul's second letter, showing his connection to the Christian community in Rome.

keyEvents.title: Part of the congregation in Rome
keyEvents.description: Eubulus is mentioned together with Pudens, Linus, and Claudia as believing brothers and sisters in Rome who supported Paul during his imprisonment.

keyEvents.title: Paul's final letter
keyEvents.description: The context for Eubulus' mention is Paul's closing words in his last known letter, written during his second imprisonment in Rome as he awaited execution.

keyEvents.title: Faithful support in difficult times
keyEvents.description: While many had abandoned Paul, Eubulus was among the believers who still kept in touch with the apostle and showed care for him in his final days.
